response.reason:
Three numbered segments describe a collision-avoidance sub-machine: (1) a cardinality obligation of three regions, (2) an activation/entry obligation triggered by three alternative collision-detection events, and (3) a region-structure/concurrency obligation that the regions support simultaneous concurrent activation of different collision-avoidance controls. I extracted: a cardinality contract for NL1 (three regions, member_domain=concurrent_regions since NL3 explicitly confirms orthogonal/parallel region semantics); an initial_entry/activation contract for NL2 capturing that the sub-machine becomes active upon one of three alternative collision events (modeled as an entry/state_action obligation with three alternative triggering events, since no exact source/target state names are given beyond the sub-machine itself, and as a region_structure/concurrency-informing containment context is not itself a distinct transition); and for NL3, a region_structure contract asserting orthogonal/concurrent region structure enabling concurrent activation of distinct controls, plus a state_action-type obligation is not warranted since NL3 does not name a continuous task but a structural allowance of concurrency. I avoided manufacturing progress or endpoint contracts for elements not named with exact source/target identities (no explicit distinct state names given in NL beyond the sub-machine and regions), keeping contracts precise, unresolved where necessary, and preserving state_role, evidence_types, and binding hints as required. No cardinality count or region evidence was invented beyond what NL1/NL3 state.</reason>

response.reason: This lens compares the NL contracts against the exact source inventory and closed FCSTM structure. The source PlantUML/canonical IR defines three sibling composites (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) under CollisionAvoidanceSystem, each with its own local [*] -> Idle initial edge, but there is no single activation transition from a root/enclosing controller into 'CollisionAvoidanceSystem (active)' triggered by any of the three collision events; the closed FCSTM instead auto-enters CollisionAvoidanceSystem unconditionally at root init. RearEnd and Pedestrian composites have malformed nested initial edges targeting a synthetic InvalidInitialtr_000X placeholder rather than a valid child state within their own scope (the PlantUML source shows [*] -> Idle inside RearEnd/Pedestrian, but the FCSTM shows the initial edge redirected to an invalid placeholder, meaning the exact owner-local edge does not reach the required target 'Idle' in that owner scope). This supports initial_entry defects for NL2-ACTIVATION-1 (activation transition triggered by events is entirely missing from the transition inventory) and for the derived containment/region-structure contracts. The three named alternatives (frontend/rear-end/pedestrian collision events) have no corresponding transitions anywhere in the complete 26-row transition inventory (only Collision_Detected/Brake_Applied/Collision_Avoided events tied to internal Frontend transitions exist, none named 'possible X collision detected'), confirming S2/S3 absence for the activation group. Region-structure: CollisionAvoidanceSystem has three sibling composite children (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) with no explicit orthogonal-region separator construct (no '--' in PlantUML, no concurrent_regions array populated in canonical IR which reports concurrent_regions count=0); NL1/NL3 both require three concurrent/orthogonal regions structurally, but the source and closed model show three sequential/exclusive sibling composite states without any orthogonal-region container, so region_structure and cardinality obligations are structurally mismatched (member_domain concurrent_regions is asserted by NL but the actual structure has zero region separators - one implicit region holds all three composites as mutually exclusive siblings, not concurrent regions). I bind cardinality owner to CollisionAvoidanceSystem (composite) as scope_concept 'this diagram'/'collision avoidance sub-machine' and preserve concurrent_regions as the NL-established primary domain per instructions, flagging structural mismatch as evidence for D. Containment (NL2-DERIVED) is satisfied: CollisionAvoidanceSystem is directly owned by the root/enclosing wrapper per tr_0013/[*]->CollisionAvoidanceSystem and FCSTM transition:line:45, so I omit that contract. I omit the deadlock/progress derived contract (NL3-DERIVED) from this lens because it is a behavior_consequence-style property better suited to that lens, but note the region-structure mismatch as the structural predicate for this lens.

result.reason: This lens compares the NL contracts against the exact source inventory and closed FCSTM structure. The source PlantUML/canonical IR defines three sibling composites (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) under CollisionAvoidanceSystem, each with its own local [*] -> Idle initial edge, but there is no single activation transition from a root/enclosing controller into 'CollisionAvoidanceSystem (active)' triggered by any of the three collision events; the closed FCSTM instead auto-enters CollisionAvoidanceSystem unconditionally at root init. RearEnd and Pedestrian composites have malformed nested initial edges targeting a synthetic InvalidInitialtr_000X placeholder rather than a valid child state within their own scope (the PlantUML source shows [*] -> Idle inside RearEnd/Pedestrian, but the FCSTM shows the initial edge redirected to an invalid placeholder, meaning the exact owner-local edge does not reach the required target 'Idle' in that owner scope). This supports initial_entry defects for NL2-ACTIVATION-1 (activation transition triggered by events is entirely missing from the transition inventory) and for the derived containment/region-structure contracts. The three named alternatives (frontend/rear-end/pedestrian collision events) have no corresponding transitions anywhere in the complete 26-row transition inventory (only Collision_Detected/Brake_Applied/Collision_Avoided events tied to internal Frontend transitions exist, none named 'possible X collision detected'), confirming S2/S3 absence for the activation group. Region-structure: CollisionAvoidanceSystem has three sibling composite children (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) with no explicit orthogonal-region separator construct (no '--' in PlantUML, no concurrent_regions array populated in canonical IR which reports concurrent_regions count=0); NL1/NL3 both require three concurrent/orthogonal regions structurally, but the source and closed model show three sequential/exclusive sibling composite states without any orthogonal-region container, so region_structure and cardinality obligations are structurally mismatched (member_domain concurrent_regions is asserted by NL but the actual structure has zero region separators - one implicit region holds all three composites as mutually exclusive siblings, not concurrent regions). I bind cardinality owner to CollisionAvoidanceSystem (composite) as scope_concept 'this diagram'/'collision avoidance sub-machine' and preserve concurrent_regions as the NL-established primary domain per instructions, flagging structural mismatch as evidence for D. Containment (NL2-DERIVED) is satisfied: CollisionAvoidanceSystem is directly owned by the root/enclosing wrapper per tr_0013/[*]->CollisionAvoidanceSystem and FCSTM transition:line:45, so I omit that contract. I omit the deadlock/progress derived contract (NL3-DERIVED) from this lens because it is a behavior_consequence-style property better suited to that lens, but note the region-structure mismatch as the structural predicate for this lens.

response.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequence: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, and dead-end facts. The closed FCSTM shows CollisionAvoidanceSystem is entered via root initial edge but its three sub-machines (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) are never entered by any exact edge - CollisionAvoidanceSystem only has a default entry to UnspecifiedInitial, not to Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian. This makes the activation contract (NL2-ACTIVATION-1) fail: no exact initial_entry edge exists from CollisionAvoidanceSystem into any of the three collision-type composites on Collision_Detected-triggering events. Consequently the Collision_Detected and Brake_Applied event consumers, while declared, are entirely unreachable from root (confirmed by inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] for both events, and verify_facts event-consumer checks refuted). This directly satisfies NL2-EVENTCOVER-1's violation. The containment contract (NL2-DERIVED) is satisfied structurally (Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian are states parented under CollisionAvoidanceSystem per inspection_equivalent_facts.states), so it is omitted. The deadlock/progress-derived contract NL3-DERIVED is evaluated: RearEnd and Pedestrian regions are entirely unreachable (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL diagnostics, verify_facts refuted reachability), so concurrent activation across orthogonal regions cannot occur at all -- this is a reachability-blocking dead end rather than a local leaf/no-outgoing fact, so I keep the candidate as a G1/reachability-flavored predicate-null W1 rather than routing through V1 (which requires a reachable leaf-without-outgoing fact, not this case, since these regions are simply never reached at all from initial). Cardinality and region-structure contracts are handled by cardinality_bindings/candidates from the structural lens; here I evaluate region_structure (NL3-REGIONSTRUCT-1) for its behavioral consequence: the model has zero concurrent_regions (canonical_source_ir concurrent_regions count=0) and the composite CollisionAvoidanceSystem/RearEnd/Pedestrian have no orthogonal separator; combined with the unreachability of RearEnd/Pedestrian, concurrent activation cannot be supported operationally, so a candidate is warranted for consequence violation distinct from the pure structural cardinality contract.

result.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequence: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, and dead-end facts. The closed FCSTM shows CollisionAvoidanceSystem is entered via root initial edge but its three sub-machines (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) are never entered by any exact edge - CollisionAvoidanceSystem only has a default entry to UnspecifiedInitial, not to Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian. This makes the activation contract (NL2-ACTIVATION-1) fail: no exact initial_entry edge exists from CollisionAvoidanceSystem into any of the three collision-type composites on Collision_Detected-triggering events. Consequently the Collision_Detected and Brake_Applied event consumers, while declared, are entirely unreachable from root (confirmed by inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] for both events, and verify_facts event-consumer checks refuted). This directly satisfies NL2-EVENTCOVER-1's violation. The containment contract (NL2-DERIVED) is satisfied structurally (Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian are states parented under CollisionAvoidanceSystem per inspection_equivalent_facts.states), so it is omitted. The deadlock/progress-derived contract NL3-DERIVED is evaluated: RearEnd and Pedestrian regions are entirely unreachable (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL diagnostics, verify_facts refuted reachability), so concurrent activation across orthogonal regions cannot occur at all -- this is a reachability-blocking dead end rather than a local leaf/no-outgoing fact, so I keep the candidate as a G1/reachability-flavored predicate-null W1 rather than routing through V1 (which requires a reachable leaf-without-outgoing fact, not this case, since these regions are simply never reached at all from initial). Cardinality and region-structure contracts are handled by cardinality_bindings/candidates from the structural lens; here I evaluate region_structure (NL3-REGIONSTRUCT-1) for its behavioral consequence: the model has zero concurrent_regions (canonical_source_ir concurrent_regions count=0) and the composite CollisionAvoidanceSystem/RearEnd/Pedestrian have no orthogonal separator; combined with the unreachability of RearEnd/Pedestrian, concurrent activation cannot be supported operationally, so a candidate is warranted for consequence violation distinct from the pure structural cardinality contract.

result.reason: Thirteen obligations derived from NL2 (activation-on-event) and NL3/NL1 (orthogonal regions / region cardinality) clauses for the CollisionAvoidanceSystem sub-machine. The exact closed-model transition inventory contains only Collision_Detected/Brake_Applied/Collision_Avoided events, an unconditional untriggered root entry into CollisionAvoidanceSystem, a default entry to a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial placeholder, zero reachable consumers for the detection events, zero concurrent regions (concurrent_regions count=0), and deterministic G1 reachability refutations for Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian. These are exact, non-predicate-dependent facts (transition/event inventories, containment, and G1 backend receipts with verdict=false) that establish violated NL2/NL3/NL1 obligations across most items. Two items (i0's predicate-null identity duplicate and i12's unresolved containment frontier) are handled per their exact supplied status: i0 duplicates i2's finding with an established reading (same exact facts); i12 is a genuinely unresolved deterministic containment frontier with no resolved identity, so it is marked unresolved. i11 (Idle collapsing across 3 blocks) is established from exact source line facts about global PlantUML state-name identity. Defeaters were assessed per obligation: unconditional-entry-as-always-active does not rebut an explicit event-gated activation obligation (defeated); declared-but-unreachable consumer does not rebut reachable-consumer coverage (defeated, per protocol); outgoing edge from UnspecifiedInitial does not rebut the exact missing-entry claim (defeated); implicit-single-region vs concurrent-region reading for NL1 cardinality is a genuine competent alternative given no explicit separator syntax is required by UML for a single region and the NL's number could be read against direct children (undercutting survives, D1); the Collision_Detected-as-generic-stand-in defeater for the entirely-absent-named-events claim is a competent alternative given the model does use one generic event across all three regions (undercutting survives).

contract_extraction.reason:
Three numbered segments describe a collision-avoidance sub-machine: (1) a cardinality obligation of three regions, (2) an activation/entry obligation triggered by three alternative collision-detection events, and (3) a region-structure/concurrency obligation that the regions support simultaneous concurrent activation of different collision-avoidance controls. I extracted: a cardinality contract for NL1 (three regions, member_domain=concurrent_regions since NL3 explicitly confirms orthogonal/parallel region semantics); an initial_entry/activation contract for NL2 capturing that the sub-machine becomes active upon one of three alternative collision events (modeled as an entry/state_action obligation with three alternative triggering events, since no exact source/target state names are given beyond the sub-machine itself, and as a region_structure/concurrency-informing containment context is not itself a distinct transition); and for NL3, a region_structure contract asserting orthogonal/concurrent region structure enabling concurrent activation of distinct controls, plus a state_action-type obligation is not warranted since NL3 does not name a continuous task but a structural allowance of concurrency. I avoided manufacturing progress or endpoint contracts for elements not named with exact source/target identities (no explicit distinct state names given in NL beyond the sub-machine and regions), keeping contracts precise, unresolved where necessary, and preserving state_role, evidence_types, and binding hints as required. No cardinality count or region evidence was invented beyond what NL1/NL3 state.</reason>

The source PlantUML/canonical IR defines three sibling composites (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) under CollisionAvoidanceSystem, each with its own local [*] -> Idle initial edge, but there is no single activation transition from a root/enclosing controller into 'CollisionAvoidanceSystem (active)' triggered by any of the three collision events; the closed FCSTM instead auto-enters CollisionAvoidanceSystem unconditionally at root init. RearEnd and Pedestrian composites have malformed nested initial edges targeting a synthetic InvalidInitialtr_000X placeholder rather than a valid child state within their own scope (the PlantUML source shows [*] -> Idle inside RearEnd/Pedestrian, but the FCSTM shows the initial edge redirected to an invalid placeholder, meaning the exact owner-local edge does not reach the required target 'Idle' in that owner scope). This supports initial_entry defects for NL2-ACTIVATION-1 (activation transition triggered by events is entirely missing from the transition inventory) and for the derived containment/region-structure contracts. The three named alternatives (frontend/rear-end/pedestrian collision events) have no corresponding transitions anywhere in the complete 26-row transition inventory (only Collision_Detected/Brake_Applied/Collision_Avoided events tied to internal Frontend transitions exist, none named 'possible X collision detected'), confirming S2/S3 absence for the activation group. I bind cardinality owner to CollisionAvoidanceSystem (composite) as scope_concept 'this diagram'/'collision avoidance sub-machine' and preserve concurrent_regions as the NL-established primary domain per instructions, flagging structural mismatch as evidence for D. Containment (NL2-DERIVED) is satisfied: CollisionAvoidanceSystem is directly owned by the root/enclosing wrapper per tr_0013/[*]->CollisionAvoidanceSystem and FCSTM transition:line:45, so I omit that contract. I omit the deadlock/progress derived contract (NL3-DERIVED) from this lens because it is a behavior_consequence-style property better suited to that lens, but note the region-structure mismatch as the structural predicate for this lens.

stage_receipts.reason:
Three numbered segments describe a collision-avoidance sub-machine: (1) a cardinality obligation of three regions, (2) an activation/entry obligation triggered by three alternative collision-detection events, and (3) a region-structure/concurrency obligation that the regions support simultaneous concurrent activation of different collision-avoidance controls. I extracted: a cardinality contract for NL1 (three regions, member_domain=concurrent_regions since NL3 explicitly confirms orthogonal/parallel region semantics); an initial_entry/activation contract for NL2 capturing that the sub-machine becomes active upon one of three alternative collision events (modeled as an entry/state_action obligation with three alternative triggering events, since no exact source/target state names are given beyond the sub-machine itself, and as a region_structure/concurrency-informing containment context is not itself a distinct transition); and for NL3, a region_structure contract asserting orthogonal/concurrent region structure enabling concurrent activation of distinct controls, plus a state_action-type obligation is not warranted since NL3 does not name a continuous task but a structural allowance of concurrency. I avoided manufacturing progress or endpoint contracts for elements not named with exact source/target identities (no explicit distinct state names given in NL beyond the sub-machine and regions), keeping contracts precise, unresolved where necessary, and preserving state_role, evidence_types, and binding hints as required. No cardinality count or region evidence was invented beyond what NL1/NL3 state.</reason>
